title: Exploring Astra’s game development capabilities — my experiment with Godot
author: Chef_GGdu14
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I’ve been experimenting with **Astra through Codex** to explore how far it can go in developing a playable game in Godot. The result is **Astra-L Survivor**, which I’ve uploaded to itch.io.

I’m sharing it here as an informal experiment in AI-assisted game development. I’m interested in exploring Astra’s ability to:

* Implement interacting gameplay systems.
* Keep the project coherent as features are added.
* Diagnose bugs and make changes without breaking existing mechanics.
* Turn feedback into improvements to the actual playing experience.

The game is a 2D survival game with automatic spells, progression, enemies, and a fusion system featuring **70 base spells and 522 fusions**. That gives the experiment plenty of interactions to examine, particularly around consistency, balance, and bugs.

[**Try Astra-L Survivor on itch.io**](https://ggdu14.itch.io/astra-l-survivor)  
Windows build, French interface.

I’d be interested in hearing from others testing Astra on games: **where does it hold up as a project grows, and where does it start to struggle?**

Feedback on this build would also help identify which parts of the result deserve closer investigation.
